TLR3 and 9 are harmful during development of sepsis-induced septic cardiomyopathies, which is mediated by C5a and/or histone-induced CM damage.

TLR3 and/or TLR9 play a role in the pathophysiology of polymicrobial septic cardiomyopathies by enhancing complement activation, which leads to histone release, which in turn, causes cardiac dysfunction by damaging cell membrane of CM.

TLR3 and/or TLR9 may be potential therapeutic targets to prevent the adverse cardiac effects of sepsis.
the TLRs are not just important in the innate immune system, but they also play a key role in the development of septic cardiac dysfunction.
